title: AI assistant adoption → weekly active minutes
teaser: Power users adopt first; a random beta invite; effect flows through automated tasks.
question: Does turning on the AI assistant make users spend more time in the product?
ask: We want the average lift in weekly active minutes.

outcome.name: weekly_active_min
outcome.meaning: average weekly active minutes, month after launch

variables.name: prior_weekly_min
variables.meaning: average weekly active minutes, month before launch

instrument.name: beta_invite
instrument.meaning: 1 = randomly selected for the early beta invite

mediator.name: tasks_automated
mediator.meaning: tasks automated per week, month after launch

hidden.name: U_push
hidden.label: team leads pushing their teams to use the product more

notes.text: Anyone could turn the assistant on. Heavy users tended to try it first.
Early beta invites were sent to a random 30% of users.
The assistant works by automating repetitive tasks.
Some team leads ran their own push to get people using the product more, and told them to try the assistant; we don't know which teams.

traps.name: Power users adopt first
traps.text: Prior usage drives adoption and usage.

traps.name: Middle step
traps.text: tasks_automated is how the assistant works; controlling for it hides most of the effect.

traps.name: Unrecorded curiosity
traps.text: Appetite for new features drives both; the random beta invite still identifies the compliers' effect.

traps.name: Unrecorded team pushes
traps.text: Team-lead pushes raised both adoption and usage; no random invite at this level, so not answerable.
